**Source:** Salvo, *Veri(dis)similitude: The Rhetorical Force Generated by VR Technology* (MA Thesis, 67 pp.)
**Generated:** 2026-06-11 (Phase 1, repurposing analysis). **Conventions:** `thesis_pages` = "Salvo N" page (1:1 with PDF). `cited_loci` = source-internal page/paragraph/section numbers the thesis points to.
**Purpose:** Every external source the thesis cites, its loci, role, and whether it bridges to an existing `corpus/index/` pipeline — so the Part-II re-grounding can verify/enrich each citation against the corpus and see which RODA pillars the thesis already shares.

## RODA-bridge summary
- **Already shared with RODA + has a corpus folder (verify/enrich here):** Heidegger BT, Burke GoM, Burke RoM, Uexküll. (Heidegger QCT/Intro/NoL have no exact folder; *Heidegger and Rhetoric* is adjacent.)
- **RODA pillars the thesis does NOT cite (= the additions the re-grounding supplies):** **Calleja, *In-Game*** (PIM/incorporation) and **Rickert, *Ambient Rhetoric*** (dwelling/recalcitrance) — both have corpus folders (`In-Game (Calleja 2011)`, `Rickert - Ambient Rhetoric`) ready to bridge. The thesis's "dwell"/"dwelling" usage (th pp.48, 62) and the unserviceable-rock recalcitrance (th pp.40–41) are the natural attach-points.
- **Aristotle** (the A0–A4 spine) is wholly absent from the thesis — the deepest gap; supplied entirely by Part I.

## Citation-integrity flags (resolve before reuse)
1. **Baudrillard** ("virtual simulacrum," th pp.13/17/18) is cited but **absent from Works Cited** and carries no locus — fix in re-grounding.
2. **Three Heidegger works beyond BT** (QCT p.3, *Introduction to Metaphysics* p.11, "The Nature of Language" p.53) are easy to miss; only BT has a clean pipeline.
3. **Burke is split across four works** (GoM/RoM/PC/LSA); only GoM/RoM have folders.
4. Loci are clean translator-page numbers (no Bekker offset issue applies).
